issue_context.title: ZAMG Integration: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'
issue_context.body: ### The problem Getting following error under integration menu two days after initial setup: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'. All sensors are offline (two different stations). It suggests to repeat the setup. ### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue? 2022.11.1 ### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core? 2022.11.1 ### What type of installation are you running? Home Assistant OS ### Integration causing the issue ZAMG ### Link to integration documentation on our website _No response_ ### Diagnostics information _No response_ ### Example YAML snippet _No response_ ### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us? _No response_ ### Additional information _No response_
comments:
The problem is a expired certificate from zamg datahub. See Issue #81664
The error message `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'.` is the result of another issue (currently working on it)

> The problem is a expired certificate from zamg datahub. See Issue #81664 The error message `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'.` is the result of another issue (currently working on it)

Thanks for your help and especially for you brilliant work!
I unfortunately have the same problem. Unfortunately, the integration is not usable.

review_comments: On line 225 I noticed we should create a task for the import flow. We shouldn't await it. Please use `hass.async_create_task`. Same goes for the weather platform.
Can the api call on line 98 raise an error?
No, it returns a list or None
If it returns `None` we can't do a membership test as we do on line 98 now.

We'll need a migration now for the entities where we've changed unique_id.

Example:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/83a6012f8061ef8c5c8d5f60cb0ded7282d0dd1e/homeassistant/components/bmw_connected_drive/__init__.py#L73-L107

Please also add tests that checks that the migration works.
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/83a6012f8061ef8c5c8d5f60cb0ded7282d0dd1e/tests/components/bmw_connected_drive/test_init.py#L20-L74

OK, but I can't use a replacement list (on import the `name` part could be anything).
A check if unique id is just a `number` without any text should sufficient.
What do you think?

The station id is the same for all of the entities of the config entry. Just check if the unique_id is not the station id for the weather entity entries, and if so, update the entity entry to set the unique_id to the station id.

What if another platform will be added in the future that requires another parameter than what the sensor platform needs? This design seems fragile. Why can't we fetch all available parameters with the coordinator by default?

The thing is that the api is not the fastest to respond on a query.
With a reduction of the api parameters we get a faster response from the api server.

I know that that is not the ideal solution for that.
